phase_name: Root-Cause Gate 8's 457s Against Its Own 103s Projection

objectives.description: Re-derive discovered suite set from run-all.sh's own discovery; compare against hint-file row count; record unhinted set
Run gate 8 standalone under the Phase 1 harness; record wall clock, per-suite timing sum, longest straggler, observed peak concurrency, resolved JOBS
Test candidate 2 directly: assert observed peak concurrent worker count against resolved JOBS
Test candidate 3 directly: re-run at --jobs 8 and --jobs 12 on a quiet host, compare against --jobs auto
Attribute the recursive component: how much of gate 8's wall clock is spent inside nested verify-deploy.sh invocations
Record the verdict table naming supported/excluded candidates, with load capture and validity marking

approaches_tried.approach: measure-gate-costs.sh --gate 8 --runs 2 at --jobs auto on what was believed to be an idle host (1.74 1-min load at launch)
approaches_tried.reason: concurrent, unrelated sibling agent activity on the same host (other active sessions were running their own builds/tests throughout this dispatch) drove the 1-minute load to 4.73-4.94 mid-run. The Phase 1 harness correctly detected this and marked the sample ALL_VALID=false (runs: 611138ms, 633802ms) rather than silently reporting a contaminated figure as trustworthy. This is exactly the hazard Phase 1 was built to catch, now observed live rather than only in Phase 1's own test fixtures.

approaches_tried.approach: monitoring live worker concurrency during the real gate-8-equivalent run-all.sh run via a /proc-descendant-count poll loop
approaches_tried.reason: the first attempt relied on the Bash tool's own 560000ms timeout parameter alone, with no explicit shell-level `timeout` wrapper around the poll loop -- the command ran past that mark and the harness auto-backgrounded it (bounded-build-waiter.md's 'Shape 3: harness-initiated backgrounding' case) instead of returning control cleanly. Recovered by checking the real target PID's liveness directly in a fresh, properly `timeout`-wrapped call rather than waiting on the harness's own completion notification for the orphaned monitor. A second, correctly-bounded 120s attempt landed too late in the run (only 2 samples, both near the tail) to be a representative peak-concurrency sample.

approaches_tried.approach: synthetic sleep-based concurrency probe: 8-12 trivial `test-zzz-concurrency-probe-N.sh` fixtures (bare `sleep 6; exit 0`), run through the real, unmodified run-all.sh scheduler at --jobs 4/8/12/auto, deleted immediately after each measurement
approaches_tried.reason: sleep is a kernel timer wait, not CPU work, so this measurement is immune to the host contention that invalidated the direct gate-8 measurement above. Reproduced the exactly-predicted wall clock for true N-way concurrency at every jobs level tested (8@--jobs4 -> ~14s = 2 waves; 12@--jobs8 -> ~15s = 2 waves; 12@--jobs12 -> ~9.5s = 1 wave; 12@--jobs-auto -> ~21s = 3 waves, confirming auto resolves to JOBS_CAP=4 not nproc=24). This conclusively refutes candidate 2 (the scheduler delivers exactly the concurrency it is asked for) and directly demonstrates candidate 3's mechanism (JOBS_CAP=4 binds, and an explicit --jobs above it does buy more concurrency) without needing an idle host at all.

deviations.description: Run gate 8 standalone under the Phase 1 harness and record wall clock, per-suite timing sum, longest straggler, observed peak concurrency, resolved JOBS
deviations.reason: the host was not genuinely idle during this dispatch's window (confirmed: two independent gate-8-equivalent attempts were both load-contaminated by concurrent sibling activity, one up to 1-min load 9.0). Live-concurrency-under-real-load was abandoned in favor of a host-load-independent synthetic sleep-probe (see approaches_tried) that answers the SAME question (does the scheduler deliver its requested concurrency?) without requiring host idleness. The per-suite timing sum, straggler identity, and nested-invocation attribution were taken from the already-idle-captured suite-cost-hints.txt (itself produced by this same Phase 1 harness under its own load gate) rather than re-captured fresh, since a fresh capture could not be trusted this session.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — live concurrency measured via a host-load-independent synthetic sleep probe instead of under the real, contended gate-8 run; see shell-script-testing.md verdict section for the full substitution rationale)*

verification.scheduler_concurrency_probe: 8 synthetic suites @ --jobs 4: 14.17s (predicted ~12-14s for 2 waves); 12 @ --jobs 8: 15.20s (2 waves); 12 @ --jobs 12: 9.51s (1 wave); 12 @ --jobs auto: 21.35s (3 waves, confirming auto=JOBS_CAP=4); 8 @ --jobs 1 baseline: 49.87s (8 serial waves, confirming probe methodology). All probe fixtures created and deleted within this phase; git status confirms no trace left.
verification.recursive_component_attribution: test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh invokes $VERIFY_DEPLOY at exactly 3 call sites (verified via grep -n '\$VERIFY_DEPLOY', not the comment-inflated grep -c count): line 175 (run_gate20() helper, --only-gate 20 scoped, invoked across a 3-iteration mode loop), line 189 (the one full-battery --skip-slow invocation, no --only-gate -- re-pays gate3 ~125s + gate22 ~55s), line 309 (deploy_findings_snapshot, --only-gate 20 scoped). Only line 189 is expensive; it alone accounts for the bulk of this suite's 228595ms idle hint, which is itself ~22% of the entire 151-suite serial-cost sum.
